items.question: In the R22 emergency procedures definitions, what does 'Land Immediately' mean?
options: Land on the nearest clear area where a safe normal landing can be performed, prepared to enter autorotation
items.explanation: 'Land Immediately' means land on the nearest clear area where a safe normal landing can be performed, being prepared to enter autorotation during the approach if required.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: DEFINITIONS (p.3-1)

items.question: What does 'Land as soon as practical' mean?
options: Land immediately in the nearest field
The landing site is at the pilot's discretion based on the problem and available areas; flight beyond the nearest airport is not recommended
items.explanation: 'Land as soon as practical' leaves the landing site to the pilot's discretion based on the nature of the problem and available landing areas; flight beyond the nearest airport is not recommended.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: DEFINITIONS (p.3-1)

items.question: What is usually the first indication of a power failure in the R22?
items.explanation: A power failure — engine or drive system — will usually be indicated by the low RPM horn.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE - GENERAL (p.3-1)

items.question: What is the immediate action for any power failure?
options: Raise collective to arrest the descent
Lower collective immediately to enter autorotation
items.explanation: In case of power failure, immediately lower collective to enter autorotation. Aft cyclic is required when the collective is lowered at high airspeed.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE - GENERAL (p.3-1)

items.question: How might an engine failure (as opposed to a drive system failure) be recognised?
options: Rotor RPM increasing while engine RPM decreases
A change in noise level, nose-left yaw, an oil pressure light, or decreasing engine RPM
No yaw and rising rotor RPM
items.explanation: An engine failure may be indicated by a change in noise level, nose-left yaw, an oil pressure light, or decreasing engine RPM. A drive system failure may show unusual noise/vibration, nose yaw, or decreasing rotor RPM while engine RPM increases.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE - GENERAL (p.3-1)

items.question: For a power failure above 500 ft AGL, what glide airspeed should be established?
items.explanation: Establish a steady glide at approximately 65 KIAS (for maximum glide distance use approximately 75 KIAS at ~90% rotor RPM).
references: R22 POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE ABOVE 500 FEET AGL (p.3-2)

items.question: During a power-failure autorotation above 500 ft, what rotor RPM band should be maintained with collective?
items.explanation: Adjust collective to keep RPM between 97 and 110%, or apply full down collective if light weight prevents attaining above 97%.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE ABOVE 500 FEET AGL (p.3-2)

items.question: During an autorotation, at approximately what height AGL should the cyclic flare begin?
items.explanation: At about 40 ft AGL begin the cyclic flare to reduce rate of descent and forward speed; at about 8 ft AGL apply forward cyclic to level the ship and raise collective just before touchdown.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE ABOVE 500 FEET AGL (p.3-2)

items.question: For a power failure below 8 ft AGL, what are the actions?
options: Apply right pedal as required to prevent yawing, allow the aircraft to settle, and raise collective just before touchdown
Roll throttle off and apply full left pedal
Push cyclic forward and land running
items.explanation: Below 8 ft AGL: apply right pedal as required to prevent yawing, allow the aircraft to settle, then raise collective just before touchdown to cushion the landing.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: POWER FAILURE BELOW 8 FEET AGL (p.3-3)

items.question: What is the maximum-glide-distance autorotation configuration?
items.explanation: Maximum glide: airspeed approximately 75 KIAS, rotor RPM approximately 90%. Best glide ratio is about 4:1, or one nautical mile per 1500 ft AGL. Increase RPM to 97% minimum when below 500 ft AGL.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: MAXIMUM GLIDE DISTANCE CONFIGURATION (p.3-3)

items.question: What is the approximate best autorotative glide ratio for the R22?
options: About 4:1 (one nautical mile per 1500 ft AGL)
items.explanation: Best glide ratio is about 4:1, roughly one nautical mile of distance per 1500 ft of height AGL.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: MAXIMUM GLIDE DISTANCE CONFIGURATION (p.3-3)

items.question: What are the R22 air restart steps (in order)?
options: Mixture full rich; primer (if installed) down and locked; throttle closed then cracked slightly; actuate starter with left hand
Battery off, fuel off, glide to landing
Carb heat on, throttle full, magnetos off then on
items.explanation: Air Restart Procedure: 1) Mixture full rich; 2) Primer (if installed) down and locked; 3) Throttle closed, then cracked slightly; 4) Actuate the starter with the left hand. Do not attempt if engine malfunction is suspected or before a safe autorotation is established.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: AIR RESTART PROCEDURE (p.3-3)

items.question: In an autorotation below 500 ft AGL, to what value should rotor RPM be increased?
items.explanation: A caution in Section 3 directs increasing rotor RPM to 97% minimum when autorotating below 500 ft AGL.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: MAXIMUM GLIDE DISTANCE CONFIGURATION (p.3-3)

items.question: In a power-off emergency water landing, when is lateral cyclic applied?
options: Before water contact to slow the aircraft
When the aircraft contacts the water, to stop the rotors
items.explanation: Follow the power-failure-over-land procedure until contacting the water (unlatch doors first if time permits), then apply lateral cyclic when the aircraft contacts the water to stop the rotors, release the seat belt and clear the aircraft.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: EMERGENCY WATER LANDING – POWER OFF (p.3-4)

items.question: In a power-ON emergency water landing, what is done before the aircraft contacts the water?
options: Descend to a hover, unlatch doors, passenger exits, fly clear, then battery and alternator OFF and roll throttle off
items.explanation: Power on: descend to a hover above the water, unlatch doors, passenger exits, fly to a safe distance, battery and alternator switches OFF, roll throttle off into the overtravel spring, keep the aircraft level and apply full collective as it contacts the water, then lateral cyclic to stop the rotors.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: EMERGENCY WATER LANDING – POWER ON (p.3-4)

items.question: How is a loss of tail rotor thrust usually indicated?
options: Nose-left yaw that cannot be corrected with right pedal
Nose-right yaw that cannot be corrected with left pedal
A total loss of collective control
items.explanation: Loss of tail rotor thrust is usually indicated by nose-right yaw that cannot be corrected (forward flight) or stopped (hover) by applying left pedal.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST (p.3-5)

items.question: What is the first action for loss of tail rotor thrust in forward flight?
items.explanation: In forward flight: immediately enter autorotation, maintain at least 70 KIAS if practical, select a landing site, roll throttle off into the overtravel spring and perform an autorotation landing.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN FORWARD FLIGHT (p.3-5)

items.question: What is the procedure for loss of tail rotor thrust in a hover?
options: Immediately roll throttle off into the overtravel spring, allow the aircraft to settle, and raise collective just before touchdown
Apply full right pedal and hover-taxi clear
Enter forward flight and continue to an airport
items.explanation: In a hover: immediately roll the throttle off into the overtravel spring and allow the aircraft to settle, then raise collective just before touchdown to cushion the landing.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR THRUST IN HOVER (p.3-5)

items.question: If headset audio fails in flight, what should the pilot do?
options: Switch the intercom to hot-mic and continue normally
items.explanation: If headset audio fails, land as soon as practical. On aircraft that provide the low RPM horn through the audio system, the pilot will not hear the horn with a failed headset.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: HEADSET AUDIO FAILURE (p.3-5)

items.question: For an engine fire during start on the ground, what should be done with the starter/cranking?
options: Continue cranking and attempt to start, which would draw flames and excess fuel into the engine
Crank for exactly 5 seconds then stop
items.explanation: Engine fire during start on the ground: continue cranking and attempt to start (this draws flames and excess fuel into the engine); if it starts, run at 50–60% RPM briefly, then mixture OFF, fuel valve OFF, battery OFF, rotor brake if time permits, and exit.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: ENGINE FIRE DURING START ON GROUND (p.3-6)

items.question: For an engine fire in flight, what is the first action?
items.explanation: Engine fire in flight: enter autorotation; cabin heat OFF and cabin vent ON if time permits; if the engine runs, perform a normal landing then mixture and fuel valve OFF; if it stops, fuel valve OFF and complete the autorotation; then battery OFF, rotor brake if time permits, exit.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: ENGINE FIRE IN FLIGHT (p.3-6)

items.question: For an electrical fire in flight, what are the first two actions?
options: Battery and alternator switches OFF, then open the cabin vents
Enter autorotation, then fuel valve OFF
Pull all circuit breakers, then reset them
items.explanation: Electrical fire in flight: battery and alternator switches OFF, open cabin vents, land immediately, fuel mixture and fuel valve OFF, rotor brake if time permits, exit.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: ELECTRICAL FIRE IN FLIGHT (p.3-6)

items.question: What is lost when the battery and alternator switches are both turned off (e.g. during an electrical fire)?
options: The low RPM warning system and the governor become inoperative
Nothing — everything runs off the battery bypass
items.explanation: A caution notes the low RPM warning system and governor are inoperative with the battery and alternator switches both off (a fused bypass still keeps the tachometers and clock powered).
references: R22 POH Sec 3: ELECTRICAL FIRE IN FLIGHT (p.3-6)

items.question: If it is unclear which tachometer is malfunctioning, or both are malfunctioning, what should the pilot do?
options: Switch the governor off and fly manual throttle
Allow the governor to control RPM and land as soon as practical
Ignore RPM and continue to destination
items.explanation: Tachometer failure: use the remaining tach to monitor RPM. If it is unclear which is faulty, or both fail, allow the governor to control RPM and land as soon as practical.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: TACHOMETER FAILURE (p.3-7)

items.question: How do the tachometers stay powered with the battery and alternator switches off?
options: A special bypass circuit lets the battery supply the tachs (with the clutch actuator switch engaged)
They run off the alternator only
A backup capacitor powers them for 5 minutes
items.explanation: Each tach, the governor and the low RPM horn are on separate power circuits; a special circuit allows the battery to supply power to the tachs with the battery and alternator switches both off.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: TACHOMETER FAILURE (p.3-7); Sec 7 DUAL TACHOMETER (p.7-23)

items.question: What is the procedure for an RPM governor malfunction?
options: Land immediately with no further action
Grip the throttle firmly to override the governor, switch the governor off, and complete the flight on manual throttle
Switch the governor off and let RPM find its own level
Reduce collective to idle and autorotate
items.explanation: Governor failure: grip the throttle firmly to override the governor, then switch the governor off and complete the flight using manual throttle control.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: GOVERNOR FAILURE (p.3-7)

items.question: The OIL warning light illuminates. What does the POH direct?
options: Land as soon as practical regardless
Check the engine tach for power loss and the oil pressure gage; if pressure loss is confirmed, land immediately
Reduce power and continue to destination
items.explanation: The OIL light indicates loss of engine power or oil pressure. Check the engine tach for power loss and the oil pressure gage; if pressure loss is confirmed, land immediately — continued operation without oil pressure causes serious engine damage.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS (p.3-8)

items.question: A gearbox chip light illuminates with no other symptoms (no noise, vibration or temperature rise). What does the POH direct?
options: Pull the associated circuit breaker and continue
items.explanation: If a chip light is accompanied by any indication of a problem (noise, vibration, temperature rise), land immediately. If there is no other indication, land as soon as practical.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS (p.3-8)

items.question: The CLUTCH light comes on in flight and does not go out within 10 seconds. What does the POH direct?
options: Pull the CLUTCH circuit breaker and land as soon as practical; land immediately and be prepared to autorotate if other drive-system symptoms are present
Cycle the clutch switch off and on
Increase RPM to re-tension the belts
items.explanation: A momentary clutch light during run-up or to re-tension warm belts is normal. If it flickers or comes on in flight and does not go out within 10 seconds, pull the CLUTCH circuit breaker and land as soon as practical; reduce power and land immediately (be prepared to autorotate) if there are other drive-system symptoms.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS (p.3-9)

items.question: The ALT caution light illuminates in flight. What is the initial action?
options: Turn off nonessential electrical equipment and cycle the ALT switch off then on after one second to reset the control unit; if it stays on, land as soon as practical
Pull the alternator field circuit breaker
Switch the battery off to protect it
items.explanation: ALT light: turn off nonessential electrical equipment and switch the alternator off then back on after one second to reset the alternator control unit. If the light stays on, land as soon as practical — continued flight without a functioning alternator can cause loss of power to the tachometers.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS (p.3-9)

items.question: The STARTER ON light stays illuminated after the ignition switch is released from Start. What is the immediate action?
options: Immediately pull the mixture off and turn the battery switch off; have the starter serviced
items.explanation: STARTER ON indicates the starter motor is engaged. If it does not go out when the ignition switch is released from Start, immediately pull the mixture off and turn the battery switch off, and have the starter serviced.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS (p.3-9)

items.question: At what rotor speed does the LOW RPM light (and horn) activate, and when is it disabled?
options: Below 97%; disabled when the collective is full down
items.explanation: The LOW RPM light and horn indicate rotor speed below 97% RPM and are disabled when the collective is full down. Recovery: lower collective, roll throttle on and, in forward flight, apply aft cyclic.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS / AUDIO ALERTS (p.3-9, 3-10)

items.question: What does the high RPM warble tone in the audio system indicate, and what is the response?
options: Rotor speed approaching the 110% limit — raise collective as required to control RPM
Engine overspeed — reduce throttle to idle
Governor failure — switch the governor off
items.explanation: On later aircraft, a warble (high/low tone) indicates rotor speed is approaching the 110% RPM limit. Raise collective as required to control RPM.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: AUDIO ALERTS – HIGH RPM WARBLE (p.3-10)

items.question: The CARBON MONOXIDE caution light illuminates. What are the actions?
options: Shut off the heater and open nose and door vents; if hovering, land or transition to forward flight; land immediately if CO-poisoning symptoms accompany the light
Increase cabin ventilation and continue to destination
Pull the heater circuit breaker and ignore it
items.explanation: CO light: shut off the heater and open the nose and door vents. If hovering, land or transition to forward flight. If symptoms of CO poisoning (headache, drowsiness, dizziness) accompany the light, land immediately.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: WARNING/CAUTION LIGHTS – CARBON MONOXIDE (p.3-9)

items.question: How long after the engine stops must the pilot wait before applying the rotor brake?
items.explanation: In the fire and electrical-fire procedures (and normal shutdown), the rotor brake is applied only after waiting — the rotor brake description specifies at least 30 seconds after the engine stops, and a stop taking less than 20 seconds may damage the brake shoes.
references: R22 POH Sec 3: ENGINE FIRE IN FLIGHT (p.3-6); Sec 7 ROTOR BRAKE (p.7-28)
